problem: Outdoor long-range VLN loses goal cues (small distant targets, occlusion, out of view), and existing memory methods (robot-centric 2D cues, implicit latent histories) go stale or blurry during traversability-driven detours. Traversability is also used only as a reject-only safety filter that offers no goal-consistent alternative.
motivation: In real terrain the remembered cue direction may be unreachable, forcing detours that prolong cue-free phases and erode memory. The paper therefore treats traversability as a stability condition for keeping goal-directed guidance, not just a local safety concern.
key_idea: Ground visibility-gated semantic bearings into executable headings via a VLM-predicted near-field traversability profile (snapping to the nearest traversable sector), and keep a world-aligned particle-filter 3D cue memory whose uncertainty-scaled cone is read out during cue-free phases.
insight: Each module addresses a different link of the guidance loop. Ablation in the Wild scene: removing the 3D memory hurts cue-free survival most (Fail@CF 72.0, CFSR@50 16.0 vs 41.0 / 52.0 for the full system). Removing traversability grounding mainly hurts path efficiency (SPL 0.22 vs 0.35). Removing cue extraction lowers SR to 32.0. World-aligned memory plus feasibility-aware grounding beats the robot-centric memory and reject-only filtering baselines. Swapping the VLM backend for traversability (Qwen3-VL, GPT-4o, Gemini) gives IoU 0.74 to 0.85, so the grounding interface is largely model-agnostic.
method: Exploration cue extraction: a Qwen VLM parses the instruction into a goal phrase and an exploration phrase; image tiles are ranked by relevance to the exploration phrase (top-K=2), and the top tile's center ray gives the exploration bearing.

Goal cue extraction with visibility gating: EzReal-style multi-scale tile scoring inside the top-K region; the goal is visible if the peakedness ratio max(s)/mean(s) exceeds 1.5, then the top tile center is back-projected to a goal bearing, else fall back to the exploration bearing.

Traversability-aware heading grounding: the view is split into N=10 sectors, the VLM scores traversability per sector, and scores are smoothed by an EMA with a running std. A sector is traversable if mu - lambda*sigma >= tau_trav (0.7 for Scout Mini, 0.5 for Go1). G(.) snaps the bearing to the closest traversable sector.

3D particle cue memory: after two visible observations from poses at least 0.5 m apart, triangulate the goal and initialise M=200 particles; update with diffusion and reprojection-likelihood weights plus systematic resampling when ESS < M/2; uncertainty is the weighted covariance trace.

Uncertainty-aware readout in cue-free phases: freeze the memory mean, compute the bearing from odometry to it, set a cone half-angle from uncertainty (15° to 60°), and ground the heading within the cone, falling back to the exploration heading if no traversable sector lies in the cone.
Three-layer runtime: VLM perception at 0.3-0.5 Hz (~2.8 s per update), guidance integration at ~1 Hz, and the native low-level controller at ~50 Hz tracking the executable heading.

setting.backbone: Qwen3-VL-4B (frozen, used for instruction parsing, tile scoring and traversability) plus a particle filter
setting.observation: monocular/forward RGB (640x480) with stereo camera and LiDAR-inertial odometry for pose
setting.action_space: executable heading (bearing) tracked by a local controller/planner
setting.simulator: Unreal Engine (custom Wild and Suburban outdoor scenes)
setting.privileged: none at test time (simulator GT visibility is used only for the Fail@CF/CFSR metrics); odometry pose is used

results: In simulation TARIC reaches SR 41.0 (Wild) and 50.0 (Suburban), against the strongest baseline EzReal at 29.0 and 33.0, and cue-free survival is much higher (CFSR@50 52.0 vs 27.3 in Wild). In the real world it achieves 40.0% SR (SPL 0.32) vs 17.5% for GPT-4o-GeNie, the strongest baseline.
limitations: Cue detection and visibility gating errors (missed small distant targets, false positives on clutter) can pull the memory to spurious locations.
Memory drifts under long cue-free stretches (50 m or more) because LiDAR-inertial odometry accumulates error without loop closure, causing wrong choices at multi-way junctions.

The VLM refreshes only every 2-3 s, so dynamic obstacles are not handled; the traversability estimate is unreliable on ambiguous terrain and can force needless detours. Evaluation uses custom scenes and only 40 real episodes.
